newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse seen rising further.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse seen rising further.

text.p: The Brussels bourse pushed into unchartered territory on Tuesday, setting a new all-time closing high, boosted by the strong overnight performance of the Dow Jones and a strengthened dollar.
"The sky remains blue," said a dealer, adding that he saw no reason for the stock market to slow down as all economic indicators pointed in the right direction.

"A lot of fundamental factors are pointing towards market development; short interest rates are low; long interest rates have dropped a few points the last couple of days; the Dow is up and the dollar is strong," a dealer said.
One trader said investors were closely following the Dow's performance, expecting the index rises in coming weeks.
But another dealer said that as the Bel-20 followed the Dow so closely it could suffer a correction if the Dow fell. Some dealers are worried that the Dow Jones is overvalued.
"The Dow's too high, if it falls we'll also burn our fingers," he said.
Cyclical stocks were the favourites in today's trade, with dealers attributing it to growing economic confidence.
"Cyclicals are carrying the market, not financials," said a trader.

The Bel-20 share index closed up 0.47 percent or 8.79 points at 1,880.7, after the Dow gained 76 points in overnight trading. The Dow rose 41 points in early Tuesday trade, but dropped 50 points after the Brussels bourse close.
Brussels volume was heavy with 3.843 billion francs of shares (Belgian shares) changing hands.
"Today's volume is a massive increase, it's more than double the average of the last couple of weeks.
People are jumping into the market, after having failed to get in during recent weeks bullish trade.
Cement maker CBR was up 3.2 percent at 2,745, helped by stronger investor interest in cyclical stocks, with retailer Delhaize rising 1.08 percent at 1,875 francs on similar news.
Polyurethane foam producer Recticel climbed 8.3 percent at 315 francs, with dealers putting the sharp rise down to investors shopping around for stocks who have trailed the indexes in recent months.
